info.title: launchroom API
info.summary: Deploy, inspect and configure launchroom projects from scripts, CI and the launchroom CLI.
info.description: Bearer tokens from Settings → API tokens (or `launchroom login`). A token is bound to one team and acts as its owner there, narrowed to its abilities. Errors are `{"error": {"code", "message"}}`; lists are `{"data": [...], "meta": {"nextCursor"}}`.

get.summary: Request analytics of every project of the token's team
get.description:
Requests per project and hour (per day for `30d`) over all environments, totals against the previous period, the split by server and the top paths across projects.

Requires the `read` ability.

get.summary: Image services with a newer release or an update in flight
get.description:
Updates in flight first, then majors and versions more than a year old. `project` narrows to one project. A scoped token sees its own project or service only. Services built from a repository never appear: they update with a deploy.

Requires the `read` ability.

parameters.name: project
parameters.description: A project id (`prj_…`) of the token's team.

post.summary: Start a CLI sign-in
post.description: Open `verificationUrlComplete` in a browser, then poll `POST /cli/sessions/token` every `interval` seconds.

post.summary: Poll for the token of a CLI sign-in
post.description: `428 authorization_pending` until approved, `403 access_denied` when denied, `410 expired_token` when expired or already picked up. The token is returned once.

get.summary: A command run and its outcome

post.summary: Cancel a queued or running command
post.description:
The container gets SIGTERM and 10 seconds. The run reads `cancelled` once the server confirms; an ended run is returned as it is.

Requires the `run` ability.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Replays return the first response (24 h); the same key for another request is refused.

get.summary: Output lines of a command run after a cursor
get.description:
`meta.cursor` is the cursor for the next page, `meta.hasMore` whether more lines are stored, `meta.finished` whether the run ended.

Requires the `run` ability.

get.summary: Follow a command run's output (server-sent events)
get.description:
Events: `lines` (the event id is the cursor), `status`, `end` (with the exit code), `reconnect`. Resume with `Last-Event-ID`.

Requires the `run` ability.

get.summary: Why a deployment failed, and how to fix it
get.description:
The explanation the dashboard shows: the known failure in plain words, the build's hint codes, the failing step with its last lines (secrets masked) and the fixes. `rule_violation` when the deployment did not fail.

Requires the `read` ability.

post.summary: Apply the fix suggested for a failed deployment
post.description:
Only the one-click fix listed in `getDeploymentFailure` (`fixes[].oneClick`). It stages the setting and deploys it when nothing else is staged; with other staged changes it only stages (`outcome: staged`). `free_disk` frees space on the server and deploys nothing. Needs the `deploy` ability too, and the role to change the service's settings.

Requires the `deploy` and `fix` abilities.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Replays return the first response (24 h); the same key for another request is refused.

get.summary: Log lines of a deployment after a cursor
get.description:
`meta.cursor` is the cursor for the next page, `meta.hasMore` whether more lines are stored, `meta.finished` whether the deployment settled.

Requires the `read` ability.

get.summary: Follow a deployment's logs (server-sent events)
get.description:
Events: `lines` (the event id is the cursor), `status`, `end`, `reconnect`. Resume with `Last-Event-ID`.

Requires the `read` ability.

post.description:
Only to a superseded deployment whose image still exists. Database migrations are not reverted.

Requires the `deploy` ability.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Replays return the first response (24 h); the same key for another request is refused.

post.description:

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Replays return the first response (24 h); the same key for another request is refused.

get.summary: Download an export with a one-use link
get.description:
The file itself (application/octet-stream), once, for the user who made the link, within 5 minutes.

Requires the `data:transfer` ability.

get.summary: One environment
Request analytics of an environment
get.description:
Requests per hour (per day for `30d`) by status class, totals against the previous period, the split by server and service, and the top paths (ids as `:id`, no query strings), referrer hosts and client classes. No addresses or user agents are stored.

Requires the `read` ability.

post.summary: Resume auto-deploy after a rollback
post.description:
A production rollback pauses auto-deploy (docs/04 §8): new pushes don't go live until it is resumed. Nothing is deployed right away.

Requires the `deploy` ability.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Replays return the first response (24 h); the same key for another request is refused.

Requires the `env:read` ability.

post.summary: Deploy a commit of a service (or redeploy it)
post.description:
Git services deploy `sha`, else the head of branch `ref`, else the head of their tracked branch, with the environment's last deployed configuration (staged changes stay staged). `redeploy: true` deploys the current commit again.

Requires the `deploy` ability.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Replays return the first response (24 h); the same key for another request is refused.

The log explorer's query: the newest lines of the range, oldest first. `meta.cursor` with `after` returns only newer lines.

Requires the `read` ability.

get.summary: Follow an environment's logs (server-sent events)
get.description:
Starts live runtime logs like the explorer's Live and renews them while the stream is open. Events: `lines` (the event id is the cursor), `reconnect`. Resume with `Last-Event-ID`.

Requires the `read` ability.

A new container from the live deployment's image, with the service's variables, network and volumes. `argv` runs without a shell; `name` runs a listed command. Follow it with GET /command-runs/{run}/output/stream.

get.summary: The commands a service lists
get.description:
The framework's standard commands from the live build, then the ones launchroom.json names (`deploy.commands`). Run one with `POST …/command-runs {"name": "migrate"}`.

Requires the `run` ability.

post.summary: Deploy the latest version of a service
post.description:
Builds and deploys the latest commit of the branch the service tracks, or resolves an image service's tag again. Refused while the service is stopped or has staged changes (deploy those with `POST /environments/{environment}/deploy`). Databases, workers and crons restart instead.

Requires the `deploy` ability.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Replays return the first response (24 h); the same key for another request is refused.

get.summary: The resolved env of a service (env pull, run)
get.description:
Resolved like a deploy from the last deployed revision. With `secrets=1`, secrets are included when the token has `secrets:read` and the role may reveal them; otherwise their keys are in `withheld`. Audited.

Requires the `env:read` ability.

post.description:
Follow it with GET /exports/{export}; once ready, make a link and download it.

post.description:
Replacing needs `confirmation` (the service slug) and takes a safety snapshot first. Follow it with GET /imports/{import}.

post.summary: Restart a running service
post.description:
Starts new containers of the live version (same image, configuration and environment, no build) through the usual rollout, one replica at a time when there are several. Refused while a deployment of the service is in progress.

Requires the `deploy` ability.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Replays return the first response (24 h); the same key for another request is refused.

post.summary: Start a stopped service
post.description:
Runs the version that was live when it stopped, with the configuration deployed last, through the usual rollout.

Requires the `deploy` ability.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

post.summary: Stop a service
post.description:
Its containers stop and its domains show a stopped page. Configuration, domains, volumes and deployments stay; unfinished deployments are cancelled. Applies at once, not as a staged change.

Requires the `deploy` ability.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Replays return the first response (24 h); the same key for another request is refused.

post.summary: Announce an upload to import
post.description:
Then send its chunks (0-based, chunkBytes each, the last one shorter) and complete it.

Requires the `data:transfer` ability.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Replays return the first response (24 h); the same key for another request is refused.

post.summary: Update an image service to a newer release
post.description:
Backs up the service's data first when backup storage is set up, then changes the image to `tag` (pinned to the digest the check saw) and deploys it, then watches it like any deploy and rolls back if it fails. `tag` must be one of the service's `candidates`; a `major` needs `releaseNotesRead: true`. Refused (422) while other changes are staged, a deployment runs, the service is stopped or held. The other environments of the project get the new image as a staged change. Needs `update` and `deploy`.

Requires the `deploy` and `update` abilities.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Replays return the first response (24 h); the same key for another request is refused.

post.description:
`value` is the header value or the whole header line. A ray that isn't from one of the team's services, or that the token's owner may not see, is one `rule_violation` answer, whatever the reason; a ray from a newer launchroom says so.

Requires the `read` ability.

AdvisoryDetailData.description: An advisory group's public record: plain text only (rendered as paragraphs and https links), references and the source.

AnalyticsAgentsData.description: Coarse client classes: browsers (a "Mozilla" user agent without a bot keyword), bots and crawlers, everything else.

AnalyticsData.description: Request analytics of an environment or one service. Status series are request counts per bucket, aligned with `timestamps` (bucket starts, UTC). `paths`, `referrers` and `agents` come from the edges' analytics windows; `pathRequests` is the traffic they cover, so the "other" row of the top routes is `pathRequests` minus the listed paths. `serversWithoutPaths` names edges that served traffic in the range but don't send paths yet (older servers). `blocked` counts requests the web firewall refused per bucket; they are carved out of `status4xx` (a blocked request is a 403 in the access log), so the classes still add up to the requests. `deploys` are the deploy markers of the range (App\Queries\DeployMarkers).

AnalyticsPathData.description: One normalised path of the top routes: ids appear as `:id`, there is never a query string. `blocked` counts requests to it the web firewall refused (from its own top paths); `status4xx` excludes them.

AnalyticsProjectData.description: One project of the team analytics overview: requests of all its environments over the range and per bucket, the previous period's requests, error shares, and its production environment for the drill-down link.

colorSlot.description: Slot 0–7 of the data palette (colour follows the project).

clientErrorPct.description: 4xx share in percent (the app's own, without blocked requests).

AnalyticsRange.description: Time ranges of the request analytics: the last hour in 10-minute buckets (the finest analytics and firewall rows), the last 24 hours and 7 days in hourly buckets, the last 30 days in daily buckets (from the daily rollups).

AnalyticsReferrerData.description: A referrer host (never a full URL) and the requests it sent.

AnalyticsSplitData.description: One server or service of the analytics split: its requests over the range, error rate and requests per bucket.

removed.description: A server that was removed (revoked) since; its name may now belong to another server.

AnalyticsTeamPathData.description: One normalised path of one project, for the team overview's top paths.

blocked.description: Refused by the web firewall (not in `status4xx`).

AnalyticsTotalsData.description: Request counts over the range and the same length of time before it. Requests include 1xx (WebSocket upgrades), which are in no status class. `status4xx` is the app's own: requests the web firewall refused are counted in `blocked` instead.

errorRatePct.description: 5xx share in percent; null without requests.

previousRequests.description: Requests of the previous period; null without any.

blocked.description: Requests the web firewall refused (carved out of 4xx).

previousBlocked.description: Blocked in the previous period; null when the firewall reported nothing then.

ApiAbility.description: What an API token may do. The single list: routes declare one (RequireTokenAbility) and self::grants() narrows the owner's role inside User::hasTeamPermission(), so a token never exceeds its owner and never reaches a permission no ability maps to (servers, members, team, exposure; backups only through the opt-in `data:transfer` on the transfer endpoints; exec only through the opt-in `run` on the command endpoints, D105, and never a console or SSH; image changes only through `update` on the app-update endpoint, D106). Values are stored on tokens: never rename one.

ApiFailureData.description: Why a deployment failed, in short: the failure class, its title and general hint (DeploymentFailureData) and the raw message. The full explanation (cause, the failing step's last lines, fixes) is `GET /deployments/{deployment}/failure`.

hint.description: What to do next, for any failure of this class.

ApiFailureExplanationData.description: A known failure in plain words (FailureCatalogue): `key` names it (stable, e.g. `port_mismatch`, `pnpm_outdated_lockfile`).

answer.description: The start of the app's answer to the health check, masked, when it says what is wrong.

ApiFailureFixData.description: A fix for an explained failure. `oneClick` fixes are applied with `POST /deployments/{deployment}/fixes/{code}` (or `command`, the CLI's line for it); the others need input only a person gives and say where (`command` when the CLI can do it, else `dashboardUrl`).

label.description: What the fix does, as the dashboard's button says it.

command.description: The launchroom CLI command that applies it, when there is one.

port.description: `set_port`: the port the app listens on.

seconds.description: `raise_health_timeout`: the start period it suggests, in seconds.

server.description: `free_disk`: the server to free space on.

ApiFailureFixResultData.description: What applying a fix did: `deploying` (staged and deployed, `deployment` is the new one), `staged` (other changes were staged too: review and deploy them together), `freeing_disk` (deploy again once the server has freed space).

ApiFailureHintData.description: A known build problem the server recognised in the build output (`code`, e.g. `pnpm-outdated-lockfile`), with its message.

ApiFailureReportData.description: A failed deployment explained like its page in the dashboard: the outcome, the catalogue's explanation when the failure is a known one, the build's hint codes, the failing step with its last log lines (masked when they were stored, ANSI removed) and the fixes, each with how to apply it.

title.description: The outcome in a few words ("Build failed", "Health check failed").

hint.description: What to do next, for any failure of this class (used when there is no explanation).

failingStep.description: The step that failed (null when no step was recorded as failed).

excerpt.description: The failing step's last lines, in order; numbers match the deployment's log.

errorLine.description: The first line of the failing step that reads like an error (also in the excerpt).

servingCommit.description: The commit still serving while this deployment failed, if any.

ApiLogExcerptLineData.description: One line of a failure's excerpt: `number` is the line's number in the deployment's log (`#L42` on its page), `error` whether it reads like an error. Text is plain (no ANSI escapes).

ApiTeamData.description: The team a token is bound to, with the owner's role in it.

ApiTokenClient.description: Where a token was created: Settings → API tokens, a CLI sign-in, or Settings → Robot tokens.

ApiTokenData.description: A token as its owner sees it (never its secret): `GET /me`, Settings → API tokens.

hint.description: `lr_pat_…a1b2`, not secret; null for tokens older than the hint.

fullAccess.description: Every ability the holder's role allows, including ones added later (D113); `abilities` is what that is now.

ApiTokenScopeData.description: How far a scoped token reaches: one project, or one service of it. `GET /me` answers it so a client (the MCP server, D112) can offer only what the token can use.

ApiTraceData.description: A decoded ray, as the trace page shows it: the request, where its time went (edge and app), the firewall's decision, the servers on its path, where it ended and the window of the service's logs around it (`logsFrom`/`logsTo`, epoch seconds, for `listEnvironmentLogs` with `q` = `requestId`).

requestId.description: The UUID the app got as X-Request-Id: search the logs for it.

path.description: The normalised path (ids as `:id`), without query string.

upstreamStatus.description: The status the app answered, only when it differs from `status`.

edgeTimeUs.description: Microseconds from receipt to the response headers.

upstreamTimeUs.description: Microseconds from the last attempt's dial to the app's response headers.

upstreamServer.description: The server the last attempt went to (the edge itself for local replicas).

host.description: The matched route's domain or deployment URL.

dashboard.description: The request went to the dashboard itself.

dashboardUrl.description: The trace page for this ray.

ApiTraceServerData.description: A server on a traced request's path.

AppUpdateResource.description: Updates of one image service in one environment: what runs, the newer releases launchroom found (`candidates`, biggest change first) and the update running now or that ended within a day (`run`). Apply one with `POST /environments/{environment}/services/{service}/update` and a candidate's `tag`; a `major` needs `releaseNotesRead`.

running.description: `v6.2.0`, or the tag when it isn't a version.

recommended.description: The candidate the dashboard offers first: the newest patch or minor.

canUpdate.description: This token may start an update (change the service and deploy).

blocker.description: Why an update can't start right now (staged changes, a deployment in progress…).

AppUpdateRunData.description: One update as the service shows it: its step, what is backed up, the deployment and, when it ended badly, what happened.

watchUntil.description: While watching: when the probation ends.

AppUpdateStatus.description: One update of an image service: backing_up → deploying → watching → succeeded; a failed backup or deployment ends as failed, a probation rollback as rolled_back, and a backup that is still running can be cancelled.

ApplyFailureFixInput.description: `POST /deployments/{deployment}/fixes/{code}`: values that override the fix's suggestion. Without them the suggested port or start period is used.

AutoUpdateMode.description: Which updates launchroom installs by itself in a service's maintenance window. Majors never: they can change settings and data. Stored on `service_instances.auto_update`; never rename a value.

CertStatus.description: A domain's certificate state as edges report it. Null on a domain: no edge has reported it yet.

ChangeEffect.description: What a staged change needs when deployed. Declared on Data properties with #[App\Data\Attributes\ChangeAffects].

ChangeItem.description: One staged change. `path` identifies the item for Discard (`services.svc_….deploy.startCommand`, `services.svc_….variables.var_…`). `before`/`after` are display strings and are never set for variables: a diff never carries values (not even ciphertexts).

CheckGateState.description: Where a push deployment stands with its commit's CI checks. Only `waiting` holds the deployment in the queue; every other state is final: `passed`, `none` (no check appeared within the grace period), `unsupported` (the git server has no checks) and `skipped` (Deploy now) let it start, `failed` and `timed_out` cancel it.

ChunkReceiptData.description: The answer to an uploaded chunk.

CliSessionData.description: A started CLI sign-in. The device code is the CLI's secret for polling; the user code is what the person compares in the browser.

CliTokenData.description: The token of an approved CLI sign-in, handed out once.

fullAccess.description: Every ability the role allows, including ones added later (D113); `abilities` is what that is now.

CommandCatalogueData.description: The commands a service lists (D105): its framework's, from the live deployment's build, then the ones launchroom.json names.

framework.description: The framework's display name ("Laravel"); null without one.

awaitingBuild.description: The live build predates framework commands: they show up after the next build.

CommandData.description: One command of a service's catalogue (D105): a framework command from the live build, or one the team named in launchroom.json. `name` is what `launchroom exec <name>` and `POST …/command-runs {"name"}` take.

danger.description: It changes data: the dashboard asks before it runs.

CommandEndEvent.description: `end` of a command's output stream: the run ended (the stream closes). `exitCode` is the container's, when it exited.

CommandLinesEvent.description: `lines` of a command's output stream (D105); the event id is `cursor`.

CommandOutputLineData.description: One line of a command's output (D105). `number` is stable for the run; `stream` is stdout, stderr or system (launchroom's own lines: pulling the image, the exit code). Stored masked; raw text, never HTML.

CommandRunData.description: One one-off command (D105), for the Commands tab, the API, the CLI and MCP. `exitCode` is the container's exit code once it exited; `error` says why it didn't run to its end. Never an env value.

finished.description: True once the run ended (succeeded, failed, timed out, cancelled or couldn't run).

name.description: The listed command it came from (`migrate`), else null.

outputTruncated.description: The output passed its limit and the rest wasn't kept.

deployment.description: dpl_…: the live deployment whose image ran.

ranBy.description: Who ran it; null once the account is gone.

viaApi.description: It came through an API token (the CLI, CI, MCP).

CommandRunStatus.description: Lifecycle of a one-off command: queued until its server leases the task, running while the container runs, then how it ended. `failed` is a non-zero exit; `error` means the command never ran to its end for a reason outside it (no server, image pull, launchroomd restarted).

CommandSource.description: Where a listed command comes from (D105): the build's framework presets or the team's launchroom.json (`deploy.commands`).

CommandStatusEvent.description: `status` of a command's output stream: sent when the status changes.

CommitCheckData.description: One CI check on a commit (a GitHub check run or commit status, a GitLab job or external status, a Gitea status; D111). `url` is the provider's page for it, when it gave an http(s) one.

CommitCheckState.description: One CI check on a commit, as launchroom reads it from the git provider: each provider's states map onto these three.

ConfigCheckData.description: A launchroom.json checked against an environment: its problems and, for a dry run, the staged changes it would produce and what the trust rules would ignore. Never carries variable values.

ConfigContentInput.description: `POST /environments/{environment}/config/validate|diff`: a launchroom.json to check against the environment. Never stored.

content.description: The file's text, as it is in the repository (≤ 256 KiB).

ConfigExcerptLineData.description: One line of a launchroom.json excerpt around a problem.

path.description: Where the project reads the file from (the suggested file name).

content.description: The file, formatted (two-space indent, sorted keys, trailing newline).

revision.description: The deployed revision it was exported from; null = the current settings (staged changes included).

ConfigFileEnvironmentData.description: One environment on Settings → Config file: the last read of its launchroom.json.

ConfigFileProblemData.description: A problem in a launchroom.json: where it is (1-based line and column, the dotted settings path users see), what is wrong, what to do, and a few lines of the file around it. Excerpts never contain a value the check refused as secret-looking (it is masked before it is stored).

href.description: The file at the read commit, at this line, on the repository's host (set when shown).

ConfigFileStatus.description: The outcome of the last read of an environment's launchroom.json.

CreateDeploymentInput.description: `POST /environments/{environment}/deployments`: a commit of a git service (`sha`, else the head of branch `ref`, else the head of the tracked branch), or `redeploy` of the current commit.

CreateVariableInput.description: Create a variable for the service (staged until deploy). Without `targets` it applies to the environment in the path only.

DataSubject.description: What an import or export reads or writes: a managed database or a service volume.

DecodeTraceInput.description: `POST /traces/decode`: the `X-Launchroom-Ray` value or its header line. Its shape is TraceCodec's to judge, so every unreadable value gets the same answer.

DeployEnvironmentInput.description: Apply the staged changes (web review sheet and `POST /environments/{environment}/deploy`). `stage`: build and start, route only on Promote.

DeployEnvironmentResultData.description: `POST /environments/{environment}/deploy`: the new revision and the deployments it started (none when no service needed one).

DeployMarkerData.description: A deploy on a time chart: when a deployment of a service finished (or started, while it runs). One shape for every chart (Metrics, Logs, Analytics, Security), built by App\Queries\DeployMarkers; `href` opens the deployment.

sha.description: Short commit SHA (7), when the deployment built a commit.

DeploymentChecksData.description: `deployments.checks`: a push deployment of an environment that deploys after checks pass. The state changes only through self::settle(), which follows CheckGateState's transition table. Also the API's `DeploymentResource.checks`.

problem.description: Why the last read failed while waiting ("GitHub didn't answer"); cleared by the next good read.

checkedAt.description: When the checks were last read (ISO 8601).

DeploymentEndEvent.description: `end` of a deployment log stream: the deployment settled with `status`.

DeploymentFailureClass.description: Why a deployment failed, shown prominently with hints.

DeploymentLinesEvent.description: `lines` of a deployment log stream; the event id is `cursor`.

DeploymentResource.description: A deployment of one service in one environment. `finished` is true once nothing more happens on its own: live (`active`), `failed`, `cancelled`, `superseded`, or `ready` (a staged deployment waiting for Promote).

checks.description: A push that waits (or waited) for its commit's CI checks; null when it didn't wait. While `checks.state` is `waiting` the deployment stays `queued`.

DeploymentStatus.description: The deployment state machine. Every status change goes through Deployment::transitionTo(), which validates against this table and emits DeploymentStatusChanged. queued → building? → releasing? → rolling_out → health_checking → [ready →] routing → active any in-flight status → failed | cancelled; queued/building → superseded (a newer deployment of the same service instance collapses older ones); active → superseded (a newer deployment went live). `ready`: a staged deployment is healthy and waits for "Promote" to route traffic to it; the previous version keeps serving meanwhile. It can be cancelled (its workloads are removed).

DeploymentStatusEvent.description: `status` of a deployment log stream: sent when the status changes; `finished` once the deployment settled.

DomainKind.description: generated (platform wildcard, sslip.io or *.localhost), custom (user-owned, on-demand TLS) and per-deployment URLs.

DownloadLinkData.description: A one-use download link: valid for a few minutes, for the user who made it.

EnvironmentKind.description: Kinds of environments: exactly one production environment per project, any number of persistent ones, ephemeral previews per PR.

EnvironmentLinesEvent.description: `lines` of an environment log stream; the event id is `cursor`.

EnvironmentResource.description: An environment; `revision` is the last deployed revision number (null before the first deploy).

ExportRunData.description: An export as the UI, the API and the CLI see it.

sizeBytes.description: Bytes received so far while preparing, the file's size once ready.

ExportRunStatus.description: Lifecycle of an export: launchroomd uploads the file (`preparing`); a complete, checked file is `ready` to download until it expires.

ExportSource.description: What an export reads: the data as it is now, or a stored backup.

FailureFixAction.description: The one-click fix an explained deployment failure offers (App\Support\Deployments\Failures\FailureCatalogue, direction.md §9). `set_port` and `raise_health_timeout` stage the setting and redeploy; `add_variable` opens the variable sheet with the name filled in; `generate_dockerfile` opens the guided sheet in Settings → Build.

FailureFixOutcome.description: What applying a failure fix did (ApiFailureFixResultData).

FindingCardData.description: One finding on the Security page: the service, the package and its fix, the advisory and its severity, the investigation line.

FindingCheckData.description: One evaluated rule (A1–A6) of a finding, as a checklist line.

FindingDeploymentData.description: The deployment whose image a finding was found in.

sha.description: Short commit SHA, or null for an image without a commit.

deployment.description: The deployment it was found in; null when that deployment is gone.

lastSeenAt.description: The latest check that still found it.

resolvedAt.description: When it was fixed (the version left the live deployment).

FindingInvestigationData.description: The latest investigation of a finding, as a line on a card.

FindingLevel.description: The two alert levels: "Action needed" notifies and leads the Security page; "Worth knowing" is listed quietly and never notifies.

ImportResultData.description: What an import left behind (from the task's DataImportResult).

ImportRunData.description: An import as the UI, the API and the CLI see it. The source label never carries a user or password.

step.description: The live progress line of the running task.

safetySnapshot.description: Whether a safety snapshot was taken first.

transferId.description: The transfer the file came from (to try again without uploading).

waitingFor.description: While holding: the services it waits for, still running.

waitingOn.description: While holding: why they still run, when it's their server (offline, busy with an earlier change).

ImportRunStatus.description: Lifecycle of an import: a safety snapshot first when replacing, then the services that use the data are held, then the task imports. Before the task starts a run can still be cancelled.

ImportSourceKind.description: Where an import reads from (protocol ImportSourceKind).

InventoryComponentResource.description: One component of a service's live image.

InventoryPackageData.description: Search results grouped by package name.

InventoryUseData.description: One version of a package and where it runs.

InvestigationCheckData.description: "What we checked": one signal and its window.

state.description: `checked`, `partial` (couldn't check, e.g. a server offline) or `skipped`.

InvestigationLineData.description: One sentence of "What we found". `network` is the client network a firewall line is about; only owners and admins get it.

InvestigationReplicaData.description: One replica of an investigation in progress.

InvestigationReportData.description: An investigation's report: what was checked, what was found (sentences with a level), the next steps and the honesty line. Stored as `security_investigations.report`; no process commands, only program paths, and client networks only in `network` (owners/admins).

honesty.default: Someone who got in can remove their traces, so a clean result doesn’t prove nothing happened. The firewall only sees requests that match its rules, and launchroom keeps request details for 7 days.

InvestigationStatus.description: An investigation: running while its container inspections run, then completed, partial (a replica couldn't be checked) or failed (nothing could be checked).

InvestigationStepData.description: One of "What to do now", mapped to an existing action.

LogEntryData.description: One line in the project log explorer (direction.md §9.8). `id` is stable (chunk id + index), `level` is guessed from the text. Text is raw and rendered as text, never HTML.

deployment.description: Short SHA (or deployment id when there's no commit).

environment.description: Environment name, in project- and team-wide searches.

serverId.description: Server public id (the detail drawer links the server).

LogLineData.description: One log line of a deployment. `number` is stable for the deployment (anchors `#L42`); `section` is the timeline step it belongs to (plan, build, release, rollout, health, route, runtime); `step` the finer build step reported by the daemon (install, build, push, …). Text is raw and rendered as text, never as HTML.

LogLineLevel.description: The level of a stored log line (`lines[].level`), guessed at ingest by LogLevel.

LogLineSource.description: Where a line in the log explorer came from: a build or release step, or a running service.

LogRange.description: Time ranges of the log explorer: the last 15 minutes up to the last 30 days, the longest log retention.

MeData.description: `GET /api/v1/me`: the token, its owner and its team, and its scope when it is limited to one project or service (null: every project).

PreviewHealth.description: A preview's current deployments in one word (PreviewList, the API's PreviewResource).

PreviewResource.description: A pull request's preview. `health` sums up its current deployments: `none` (no environment), `building`, `live` (every service live), `failed` (one failed), `stopped` (nothing deployed). `deployments` are the current deployment of each service; a preview has settled for `headSha` when each of them is `finished` and built from it.

PreviewStatus.description: Lifecycle of a pull request's preview. skipped / awaiting_approval / queued → preparing → running → closed | expired - skipped: filtered out (target branch, label, `[skip preview]`, fork policy off); re-evaluated on the next PR event. - awaiting_approval: a fork PR whose author lacks write access. - queued: allowed, but the project has `max_concurrent` previews running. - preparing: the environment exists; its databases start (and are cloned and sanitized when configured) before the apps deploy. - running: the apps' deployments were created (their own statuses tell the rest); synchronize events deploy new commits here. - failed: preparation failed (e.g. the clone's restore); the environment stays for inspection until the PR closes or the preview expires. - closed / expired: torn down (environment deleted). A reopened PR starts over. A preview holds a slot of `max_concurrent` while it has an environment (`environment_id`), whatever its status (e.g. awaiting approval of a fork's new commit while the approved one keeps running).

ProjectResource.description: A project with its environments (previews included).

PromotionClass.description: How a field behaves when promoting configuration between environments. Declared on Data properties with #[App\Data\Attributes\Promotion].

ResolvedEnvData.description: The resolved env of a service. `withheld` lists secret (or secret-tainted) keys left out because the token or the role may not read secrets, or `secrets=1` wasn't asked.

SecurityFindingStatus.description: Lifecycle of a finding: open → resolved (the live deployment no longer has the version, the advisory was withdrawn, the instance was removed) or dismissed ("Not affected"); dismissed → open (reopened by a user, or when the level rises or the advisory becomes known exploited) or resolved; resolved → open (the version came back).

SecurityServiceRefData.description: Where something runs: a service in a project's environment, with the link to its panel.

logo.description: Logo key of the service (`nextjs`, `postgres`, …) or null.

ServerRole.description: What a server is used for. A server has a set of roles.

ServerStatus.description: Lifecycle of an enrolled server. pending_approval → online (approved) | revoked online ⇄ unreachable → offline → online revoked is terminal: the key is denied immediately.

ServiceActionInput.description: Body of `POST …/services/{service}/stop|start|restart` (D68). `processes`: an app's workers and crons stop, start or restart with it.

ServiceActionResultData.description: `POST …/services/{service}/stop|start|restart` (D68): the service after the action and the deployments it started (Start and Restart roll out a deployment per service; Stop starts none).

ServiceInventoryResource.description: The inventory of a service's live image.

ServiceResource.description: A service in one environment. `status`: `stopped` while it is stopped (D68), else the latest deployment's status while it runs, else `live` when a deployment serves, else the latest deployment's outcome, else `not_deployed`.

stoppedAt.description: When it was stopped (null: not stopped).

Severity.description: Severity of an advisory group: the GHSA label, else the highest CVSS v3 base score, else unknown.

StartAppUpdateData.description: Update a service to one of its available releases. The tag must be a candidate of the service's latest check; a major needs the release notes read.

StartCliSessionInput.description: `POST /cli/sessions`: what the CLI says about itself; shown to the person approving (display only, never trusted).

StartCommandRunInput.description: Run a one-off command (D105): an `argv` or the `name` of a listed command, not both. The timeout defaults to 10 minutes.

argv.description: The program and its arguments, e.g. ["php", "artisan", "migrate:status"].

name.description: A command of the service's catalogue (`GET …/commands`), e.g. "migrate".

timeoutSeconds.description: Seconds before the command is stopped (10 to 3600).

StartExportInput.description: POST …/exports: the data as it is now, or a backup snapshot.

StartImportInput.description: POST …/imports: exactly one of transfer and sourceUrl.

StreamReconnectEvent.description: `reconnect`: the stream reached its maximum length; resume from `cursor` (also the event id, so `Last-Event-ID` does it).

TeamAnalyticsData.description: Request analytics of every project of a team: totals against the previous period, requests per project and bucket (aligned with `timestamps`), the split by server and the top paths across all projects (`pathRequests` is the traffic the path data covers).

TeamRole.description: Team membership roles and the role matrix. This is the only place that maps roles to permissions.

TraceFailure.description: Why the edge couldn't get an answer from the app: the byte value of the trace's `failure` field.

TraceFirewallData.description: What the web firewall decided about a traced request.

TraceFirewallOutcome.description: What the web firewall decided about a traced request.

TraceOrigin.description: Who produced the response of a traced request: the byte value of the trace's `origin` field.

TraceStop.description: Where a traced request ended on its path: the edge answered itself, the firewall gate on the edge refused it, the way to the app server failed, or the service answered.

TransferData.description: A transfer as the UI, the API and the CLI see it. Never carries keys, digests of chunks or link tokens.

format.description: protocol DataFormat: postgres_custom, postgres_sql, mysql_sql, mongodb_archive, clickhouse_backup, redis_rdb, tar, zip

topFolder.description: The archive's single top folder, when it has one (volume imports).

TransferDirection.description: Which way a transfer's file travels: an upload (browser or CLI → dashboard → launchroomd) or a download (launchroomd → dashboard → browser or CLI).

TransferStatus.description: Lifecycle of a transfer: chunks arrive (`receiving`), the complete, checked file is `ready`; `failed` and `expired` files are deleted.

UpdateCandidateData.description: A newer release of a running image, stored in `app_update_checks.candidates` and shown on the service. `digest` is what an update pins; `firstSeenAt` starts the automatic-update settle time.

tag.description: The tag to run (`v6.3.0`, `6.72.0-alpine`; for a build, the running tag).

version.description: For people: `v6.3.0`, or for a moving tag the version it names now, else the tag.

curatedBy.description: The template that pins this version (tested by launchroom).

UpdateCheckStatus.description: The outcome of the latest version check of a service instance.

UpdateKind.description: What an available release changes: the first number (major), the second (minor), a later one (patch), or nothing but the image behind the same tag (build).

UpdateVariableInput.description: Change a variable in this environment only. Omitted fields stay.

VariableResource.description: A variable row that applies to the service in this environment. Secret values are never part of it.

VariableTargetData.description: One target of a variable: an environment (public id) or "all previews", optionally only for branches matching a glob.

VariableType.description: Variable types: config values are readable by anyone who can see the service; secrets are write-only after saving.

WafMode.description: The web firewall of a service instance. Off sends nothing (RouteSpec.waf omitted); log and block are the protocol's modes.

WafRuleData.description: A CRS rule id with its message and category.

WafServiceCountData.description: A service in "Most targeted" or "Watching, not blocking yet".

settingsUrl.description: POST target of "Turn on blocking" (Log only services).

WafSummaryResource.description: `GET /api/v1/security/waf?range=`: firewall totals, per category and per service. No client networks.

code.description: unauthenticated, forbidden, missing_ability, not_found, method_not_allowed, conflict, validation_failed, rule_violation, idempotency_key_reused, idempotency_key_in_progress, rate_limited, server_error; CLI sign-in: authorization_pending, access_denied, expired_token.

ability.description: The ability the token is missing (missing_ability).

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page.

Unauthenticated.description: The token is missing, expired or revoked.

Forbidden.description: The token lacks the ability (missing_ability), or the owner's role doesn't allow it (forbidden).

NotFound.description: Not found, or it belongs to another team.

Invalid.description: Invalid input (validation_failed) or a refused operation (rule_violation).
